name: H-JACOBI-FROBENIUS-GUE-ASYMPTOTICS
domain: Arithmetic Monodromy & Katz-Sarnak USp(2g) Large-Genus GUE Spectral Bridge

hypotheses.description: Quadratic Level Repulsion (Wigner Surmise / GUE): For large genus g in {20, 50, 100}, the unfolded positive Frobenius eigenphases theta_j in (0, pi) of the symplectic monodromy group USp(2g) exhibit true level repulsion: the fraction of scaled nearest-neighbor spacings s < 0.2 satisfies P(s < 0.2) <= 0.03 (vs Poisson baseline P_Poisson(s < 0.2) = 1 - e^{-0.2} = 0.1813), and P(s < 0.05) <= 0.002 (vs Poisson 0.0488).

Montgomery-Odlyzko GUE Pair Correlation Agreement: The unfolded pair correlation function R_2(s) of the USp(2g) spectrum converges in the bulk to the GUE curve 1 - (sin(pi*s)/(pi*s))^2 with root-mean-square deviation RMSD(GUE) strictly less than half of RMSD(Poisson) across s in [0.2, 2.0].
hypotheses.threshold: RMSD_GUE < 0.5 * RMSD_Poisson for s in [0.2, 2.0] at g = 100

hypotheses.description: Symplectic Hard-Edge Origin Repulsion: As s -> 0+ (distance of the lowest eigenvalue theta_1 to the origin 0), the distribution follows the symplectic Bessel kernel scaling with strict suppression of near-zero eigenangles: P(theta_1 < 0.1 * (pi / g)) <= 0.02.
Spectral Form Factor Dip Recovery: The discrete spectral form factor K(tau) of USp(2g) exhibits the universal GUE ramp and correlation hole with min_{tau in (0, 0.4)} K(tau) <= 0.15.

methodology.computation: Quaternion-symplectic Haar measure on USp(2g) / Jacobian Frobenius monodromy
methodology.unfolding: Uniform mean density rho = g / pi on the interval (0, pi)
methodology.pair_correlation: Double-sum over distinct eigenphase pairs normalized by g and bin width ds
